Linear Systems
Linear systems are a class of systems for which the sensor, agent, and environment
models are linear functions of the continuous state, action, observation, and disturbance.

🤔So what are these nice set representations?
Set Propagation Techniques
🤔So what are these nice set representations?
1
Finite representations: we should be able to specify all the points in the set without enumerating them all.
2
Efficient set operations: e.g. linear transformation, Minkowski sum, intersection.
3
Closed under set operations: a set representation is closed under a set operation if
applying the operation results in a set of the same type.
e.g. the intersection of two rectangles is also a rectangle:
so we say that rectangles are closed under intersection.
Are they closed
under union?
Nope!
Set Propagation Techniques
🤔So what are these nice set representations?
Convex sets tend to be nice.
A set P is convex if αp+(1−α)q∈P for all p,q∈P and α∈[0,1].

Zonotopes are a special type of polytope.
They are represented as the Minkowski sum of a set of line segments centered at a point c.
Z={c+i=1∑m​αi​gi​∣αi​∈[−1,1]}
represented as center and a list of generators:
Z=(c,⟨g1:m​⟩)

But what does this do to our guarantees?
If the overapproximate reachable set does not intersect with the avoid set, we can conclude that the system is safe.
If the overapproximate reachable set does intersect with the avoid set, we cannot conclude anything.
